note: Built from sourced research on Sept 30 2026, refreshed Oct 3 and Oct 5, and the site's own records. Confirmed means a source states the date; likely means a statute or past pattern sets it.

items.title: Board of Contract and Supply: the contract for the next citywide revaluation
items.why: Item #53977: Vision Government Solutions, $2,044,000, for a full revaluation as of Dec 31, 2027.

items.title: Special Committee on Ways and Means meets
items.why: Agenda not yet posted as of Oct 5.

items.title: Public Works Committee: resolution opposing Brown's demolition of houses on Brook Street
items.why: Item #53081. Comes six weeks before the City Plan Commission hearing on the economics building.

items.title: Ordinance Committee meets
Early in-person voting begins
items.why: Runs through Nov 2.

items.title: City Council meets
items.why: The outgoing council; posted on the City calendar. By the usual pattern after that: Nov 5, Nov 19, Dec 3, Dec 17.

items.title: Brown reports its fiscal 2026 endowment return
items.why: The last year at the 1.4 percent federal endowment tax rate; it rises to 4 percent from fiscal 2027.

items.title: City Plan Commission filing deadline for the Nov 17 meeting
items.why: Brown's master plan amendment has to be filed by now to be heard Nov 17.

items.title: City Plan Commission, October meeting
items.why: The same day is the filing deadline for the Nov 17 meeting, when Brown's amendment is expected.

items.title: Second-quarter property tax due
items.why: Grace period to Oct 31.

items.title: Winter utility shutoff protections begin
items.why: Heating customers with balances under $500 are protected; arrears build until spring.

items.title: General election: mayor, all 15 council seats, Question 7
items.why: David Morales faces the general election for mayor; Question 7 would bar city investments tied to genocide or apartheid.

items.title: General election: governor, attorney general, legislature, $600 million in state bonds
WaterFire season finale
State revenue and caseload estimating conferences
items.why: Sizes the state's fiscal 2028 gap a week after the election.

items.title: Deadline to appeal your property assessment
items.why: Appeals go to the Tax Assessor’s Office in writing; state law sets the window.

items.title: City Plan Commission: Brown's master plan amendment for an economics building at Brook and Charlesfield
items.why: Two houses on Brook Street would be offered for relocation or demolished. Brown has said it will not give a housing count before the hearing. The date is the one Brown is aiming for.

items.title: One year since the shooting at Brown
items.why: Brown's safety action plan runs through 2026–27.

items.title: Tax assessment date; the City's fiscal 2026 audit is due
items.why: Providence has filed audits late before.

items.title: CharterCARE's second back-tax installment to the City
items.why: The first of 17 quarterly payments ($218,937) was due Oct 1, toward about $3.7 million of the $10.29 million Prospect owed for 2024 and 2025. Whether it was paid has not been reported.

items.title: State minimum wage rises to $17; income-tax surcharge on millionaires begins
New mayor sworn in; new council elects a president
items.why: First Monday of January, by past practice.

items.title: Governor inaugurated; General Assembly convenes
Third-quarter property tax due
items.why: The first tax deadline under the new mayor.

items.title: New governor's fiscal 2028 budget due
items.why: State law gives a newly inaugurated governor until the first Thursday in February.

items.title: City pension valuation as of July 1, 2026
items.why: The last one put the plan at 31.4 percent funded.
